title: The Speaker Played One Pure Sound, Yet Opening Their Eyes Flipped the Syllable
description:
Behavioral & Circuit Analysis — McGurk & MacDonald (1976): Hearing Voices Your Ears Never Received — How Vision Rewrites Speech ('BA' + 'GA' = 'DA'), grounded in Harry Mcgurk, John Macdonald (1976) (Nature). Empirical findings show that in 1976 at the University of Surrey, Harry McGurk and John MacDonald were testing how infants respond when a mother's voice comes from a different spot than her face, and asked a video technician to dub the sound 'ba-ba' onto a close-up film of a woman's lips pronouncing 'ga-ga'.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how cochlea, temporal lobe, auditory cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that when McGurk and MacDonald played the dubbed video back, neither heard 'ba' OR 'ga' — both swore the loudspeaker was clearly saying 'DA-DA'. They scolded the technician for mixing up the audio until they closed their eyes — and the exact same speaker instantly said 'BA-BA'.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Harry Mcgurk, John Macdonald (1976). Hearing lips and seeing voices. Nature. https://doi.org/10.1038/264746a0
- Audrey R. Nath, Michael S. Beauchamp (2012). A neural basis for interindividual differences in the McGurk effect, a multisensory speech illusion. NeuroImage. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2011.07.024
- Agnès Alsius, Jordi Navarra, Ruth Campbell, Salvador Soto-Faraco (2005). Audiovisual Integration of Speech Falters under High Attention Demands. Current Biology. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2005.03.046
